title: GENERAL INFORMATION
summary: Key to the symbols used on every AIM sheet: model 19000 means all models; a boxed number is a cross-reference, a numbered triangle is a torque (see the torque legend), a circled number is a revision, a half-filled circle marks RPO (option) parts installed like regular production, a tag such as '1a' is an applied material (grease, sealer, adhesive) listed in UPC 0, a 'Ref.' box above the sheet number points to related sheets, and a half-black square marks an existing item or part of an assembly.
notes: MODELS: SHEETS DESIGNATED 19000 REPRESENT ALL MODELS RELEASED FOR PRODUCTION
notes_internal: Title block drawing number 3965172; DR DP/C1, CK 4-18-69 C1, PREL 3-24-69, C/O A3; model 19000. Revision record is empty.
Symbol column in the table describes the glyph in words; the page shows pictures.
